questions.question: In which year was the Indian Parliamentary Group established?
questions.solution: The Indian Parliamentary Group (IPG) is an autonomous body established in 1949 following a motion in the Constituent Assembly (Legislative) in 1948. The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is its ex-officio President.

questions.question: If the State government dissolves the Panchayati Raj Institutions before the end of their term, fresh elections should be held within _____.
questions.solution: According to Article 243E, if a Panchayat is dissolved before its five-year term expires, elections to constitute the new Panchayat must be completed within six months from the date of dissolution.

questions.question: The detention of a person cannot exceed ________ unless an advisory board reports sufficient cause for extended detention.
questions.solution: Under Article 22 of the Constitution, a person cannot be kept under preventive detention for more than three months unless an Advisory Board (consisting of High Court judges) finds sufficient cause for extension.

questions.question: When was the National Emergency declared for the first time in India under Article 352?
questions.solution: The first National Emergency was declared in October 1962 due to Chinese aggression (external aggression) and remained in force until January 1968.

questions.question: Which freedom fighter was elected as the Home Minister in 1955 and abolished the Zamindari System in Uttar Pradesh?
questions.solution: Govind Ballabh Pant was a key leader in the Indian independence movement. He served as the first Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh (where he abolished the Zamindari system) and later became the Union Home Minister in 1955.

questions.question: As per the coding convention of the India Census, how many digits are used for the State code?
questions.solution: In Census coding: State (2 digits), District (3 digits), Sub-district (5 digits), and Village/Town (6 digits). For example, state codes range from 01 (Jammu & Kashmir) to 35 (Andaman & Nicobar).

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Emblem of India:
A. It was adopted on 26th January 1950.
B. It features the motto “Satyameva Jayate” from the Mundaka Upanishad.
Which is correct?
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. The State Emblem of India is an adaptation of the Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath. It was adopted the day India became a Republic. The motto 'Satyameva Jayate' is written in Devanagari script below the profile of the Lion Capital.

questions.question: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act 2009 came into force in which year?
questions.solution: Although the Act was passed in 2009, the RTE Act officially came into effect on April 1, 2010. It made education a fundamental right under Article 21A for children aged 6 to 14.

questions.question: In which year was the States Reorganisation Act enacted to reorganize the boundaries of Indian states along linguistic lines?
questions.solution: The States Reorganisation Act, 1956 was enacted following the recommendations of the Fazal Ali Commission. It reorganized India into 14 states and 6 union territories.

questions.question: The Indian Forest Act 1927 was enacted after repealing which of the following acts?
questions.solution: The Indian Forest Act, 1927 repealed the previous Indian Forest Act of 1878. It aimed to consolidate the law relating to forests, the transit of forest-produce, and the duty leviable on timber.
